# Results — Study 529 (Inventory-Growth) on the real Yahoo tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: annual inventory
growth scaled by lagged total assets, from Yahoo `balance_sheet` filings; forward returns
from daily adjusted closes. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

**Definition** (Thomas & Zhang 2002; Belo & Lin 2012):

- INVG_t = (Inventory_t − Inventory_{t-1}) / Total_Assets_{t-1}

**Reporting lag**: fiscal-year-y inventory growth → calendar-year y+1 stock return (one
documented execution lag; no look-ahead, no same-bar fill).
**Universe**: 40-name inventory-heavy survivor basket (retail, consumer staples,
industrials, autos); 37 names carry a usable INVG signal.
**Predicted trade**: long low-INVG quintile, short high-INVG quintile.

## Data stamp

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | Yahoo Finance `balance_sheet` (Inventory, Total Assets) + daily adjusted close |
| Cache | This study's own `_cache/` (`inv_balance_sheets.parquet`, `inv_prices.parquet`) |
| Basket | 40 requested / **37 with usable INVG** (survivorship-biased) |
| Signal years (with valid INVG) | 2023 (21 names), 2024 (37), 2025 (37), 2026 (16) |
| **Usable hedge years** | **2** (2023, 2024) — see limitation below |
| INVG fingerprint | `044108b907ab` |

> **DATA LIMITATION (named, not hidden)**: Yahoo's `balance_sheet` serves only ~4–5
> fiscal years of annual statements per name. After the one-year reporting lag and the
> complete-calendar-year forward-return filter, only **two** signal years (2023, 2024)
> have a fully-formed hedge return. Two annual observations cannot certify or refute the
> anomaly — this thinness is the honest reason the verdict is None/Mirage rather than a
> confident replication.

> **SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the basket is inventory-heavy names *still trading in
> 2026*. Firms that over-built inventory and subsequently failed — exactly the names the
> anomaly is built around — are absent. All results are upper bounds.

| **Q1 (low INVG — disciplined)** | **+17.3%/yr** | +1.06 | +2.99 | 100% |
| Q2 | −5.9%/yr | −1.53 | −4.32 | 0% |
| Q3 | +12.3%/yr | +1.66 | +4.69 | 100% |
| Q4 | +21.1%/yr | +6.79 | +19.22 | 100% |

| Equal-weight market | +11.3%/yr | +3.12 | +8.84 | 100% |

*(Per-quintile t-stats over n=2 years are meaningless on their own — shown only to
display the absence of any monotone low→high pattern.)*

## Placebo / label-shuffle null (1000 shuffles)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Real hedge mean | +4.6%/yr |
| Null hedge mean | +0.6%/yr |
| Null hedge std | 13.2%/yr |
| **One-sided placebo p-value** | **0.376** |

The real hedge is *inside* the noise of randomly-relabelled INVG sorts — p = 0.38, far
from any conventional significance threshold.

## Synthetic positive control (seed-robust, 20 seeds) — engine faithfulness only

| Planted premium | Mean hedge | Mean HAC t | Frac(t > 2) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.1%/yr | −0.22 | 5% |
| −0.03 | +8.3%/yr | +6.59 | 100% |
| −0.06 | +16.7%/yr | +13.40 | 100% |
| −0.10 | +27.9%/yr | +22.49 | 100% |

The engine recovers a planted inventory-growth premium reliably (t > 2 in 100% of seeds)
and returns a near-zero t under the null (5% false-positive rate ≈ nominal). The method
is faithful — so the flat real-tape result is a statement about the data, **not** the
machinery. *This control is a power check only; it is never cited to support the real
stamp.*

## Year-by-year

| Year | n | Q1 (low) | Q5 (high) | Market | Hedge |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2023 | 21 | +28.8% | +5.9% | +13.8% | **+22.9%** |
| 2024 | 37 | +5.7% | +19.4% | +8.7% | **−13.7%** |

The hedge *flips sign* between the only two years available — exactly the pattern a
two-observation sample produces when there is no underlying signal.

## Verdict

The predicted inventory-growth effect (high INVG → low returns) **cannot be certified on
this tape**. The long-low/short-high hedge earns **+4.6%/yr gross (HAC t = 0.50)**,
survives the label-shuffle placebo with **p = 0.38**, and nets **+4.0%/yr** — none of it
distinguishable from zero. The signal flips direction between the only two usable years.

The dominant obstacle is data depth: Yahoo serves too few annual balance sheets to build
a panel long enough to test a cross-sectional fundamental anomaly. Belo & Lin (2012) and
Thomas & Zhang (2002) document the effect on decades of Compustat data across the full US
cross-section; a 2-year, 37-name survivor slice is not a fair test.

- **Signal — NONE** (hedge t = 0.50, placebo p = 0.38, sign flips year-to-year; only 2
  usable years; literature supports the effect on a broad point-in-time universe, not on
  this thin survivor slice — literature support alone is never REAL).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (no signal to trade; net +4.0%/yr at t = 0.44 over 2 years;
  the survivor basket excludes the very over-builders that drive the anomaly).
- **Data depth — INSUFFICIENT** (the honest third axis: ~4 balance-sheet years per name
  from Yahoo → 2 usable hedge years; the anomaly is untestable here, not disproven).
